correctness.rationale: The defining full text proves that every unit isosceles-orthogonal pair in a symmetric Minkowski plane is represented by the one-parameter function Phi(t). The regular octagonal norm satisfies the required axis symmetries. Exact facet comparison on 0<=t<=1 produces four rational pieces separated by d=5sqrt(2)-7, a=sqrt(2)-1, and c=(5sqrt(2)-1)/7. Their derivatives have signs +,+,-,-, so the unique maximum on [0,1] is t=a. The exact reciprocal identity Phi(t)=Phi(1/t) gives the second ratio sqrt(2)+1 and no others. The displayed unit pair attains the resulting value (3+2sqrt(2))/5.
risks: The global pair classification uses the published symmetric-Minkowski theorem; it was inspected directly in the full text rather than inferred from an abstract.
The checker does not use finite sampling as a proof of the continuum maximum; the derivative argument is analytic.

originality.rationale: The defining arXiv full text was inspected through the definition, its concrete square and hexagonal examples, the James-constant comparison, and the complete symmetric-Minkowski reduction. Targeted in-document searches found no octagon, octagonal, or regular-polygon computation. published-finding corpus searches covered exact Omega notation, isosceles-orthogonal aliases, the regular-octagonal object, the candidate radical value, and the symmetric-Minkowski formulation. The closest public records compute different constants on the same octagonal norm. A 2022 article with nearly the same title was separately checked because of a notation collision: its public metadata describes a different parameterized Omega_X(alpha) invariant.
residual_risks: Bibliographic and semantic-index searches cannot establish absolute novelty.
An equivalent octagonal calculation may appear under a linearly equivalent normalization or without the Omega notation.

The 2022 parameterized Omega_X(alpha) article was not used as scientific coverage because its public description is a distinct invariant; a hidden specialization in its unavailable full text remains a low residual literature risk.
risks: No independent human literature audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The defining paper develops a special one-parameter theory precisely for symmetric Minkowski planes and demonstrates the invariant on the square and a canonical hexagonal plane. The regular octagon is the next canonical fourfold-symmetric polygonal norm and is substantially closer to Hilbert geometry; its exact value supplies a natural benchmark rather than an arbitrary slice. The calculation also identifies the maximizing vertex ratios and gives a complete reduced objective with a genuine active-facet phase structure, so future regular-polygon calculations can be compared against an exact nontrivial case.
risks: The contribution is an exact canonical benchmark and maximizer analysis, not a general formula for every regular polygon.
